gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-hind: Cheerful and youthful, KG Happy has chunky diagonals and a dominant x-height that make it feel like a grin. Hind follows in a plain sans with open, steady strokes, comfortable for a few paragraphs before you'd want a break.
gen-dafont-kg-happy-fs-technor: Cheerful, closed-up handwriting in KG Happy meets Technor's glowing neon-tube lines, where every bowl stays wide open. That open-versus-closed split is the whole story.
gen-dafont-kingthings-exeter-fs-rowan: Kingthings Exeter sets a traditional, historical tone with squeezed letter pairs and terminals cut well short of the bowl. Rowan's generous curves keep the reading friendly.
gen-dafont-klaudia-fs-plein: Loose, luxurious pen strokes with one fixed line thickness, never swelling or thinning, make Klaudia look casually handwritten. Plein steps in beneath with a reliable, clean sans whose round letters have a clear channel into each bowl, built for brief stretches of reading.
gen-dafont-klaudia-fs-spline-sans: Flowing, pen-written Klaudia looks casual yet luxurious, with wide-set terminals on its s. Spline Sans backs it up as a plain sans with open curves and identical vertical and horizontal weight, better for brief copy than for pages.
gen-dafont-klaudia-fs-synonym: Klaudia's skeleton outline keeps one fixed stroke thickness, so its flowing pen-written letters stay casually luxurious. Synonym takes over where size is big and the words are few, leaving the rest to its constant ink and generous curves.
gen-dafont-klaudia-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans is modern and precise, built from monoline strokes with curve endings kept well apart. Beneath Klaudia's flowing script it reads crisply, though a sans like this isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-dafont-klaudia-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk reads neutral and geometric, its counters breathing like a hollow reed and each glyph a ribbon of constant width. Beside it, Klaudia's flowing script adds casual luxury up top, and the two do best on brief copy.
gen-dafont-london-fs-paquito: London brings authority and drama, with very tight sidebearings and ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Paquito follows in a confident, approachable serif with little gap between x-height and caps, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-dafont-maxwell-fs-neco: Neco is an authoritative, dignified serif whose strokes swell measuredly from hairline to stem, and its letters never seem to pinch shut. Maxwell, with a single constant stroke width, is best for a handful of lines.
